front: ACCURATE mnemonic for qualities of good information
back: Accurate, Complete, Cost-beneficial, User-targeted, Relevant, Authoritative, Timely, Easy to use.

front: TPS vs MIS vs EIS vs ERP
back:
TPS: records routine daily transactions (operational).
MIS: summarises internal data into regular structured reports (tactical/middle mgmt).
EIS: internal + external summarised data with drill-down for senior executives (strategic).
ERP: single integrated database across all functions.

Intranet: private internal network restricted to employees.
Extranet: extends controlled access of an intranet to authorised external stakeholders (suppliers, travel agents, key customers).
Volume (scale of data), Velocity (speed of generation/processing), Variety (structured & unstructured formats), Veracity (trustworthiness/quality) — plus Value.

front: Descriptive vs Predictive vs Prescriptive Data Analytics
back:
Descriptive: what happened?
Predictive: what is likely to happen?
Prescriptive: what actions should we take to optimise outcomes?

front: Direct vs Indirect vs Prevention vs Appraisal Security Controls
back: Preventive controls stop errors/breaches before occurrence (passwords, encryption, firewalls, locks). Contingency/corrective controls aid recovery (backups, disaster recovery).
Unit-level (per unit), Batch-level (per setup/order), Product-sustaining (per product line/design), Facility-sustaining (general factory/rent).

Target Cost = Competitive Market Selling Price − Desired Profit Margin.
Cost Gap = Estimated Current Product Cost − Target Cost.
Closed via Value Analysis / Value Engineering (removing non-value-adding features without cutting perceived quality).
Tracks all costs over a product’s entire life (R&D, design, manufacturing, marketing, distribution, decommissioning) rather than period-by-period. ~80–90% of costs are committed at the design stage.

front: Throughput Accounting: Throughput Return per Bottleneck Hour
back:
Throughput = Selling Price − Direct Material Cost ONLY (all other factory costs including direct labour are treated as Total Factory Costs / Operating Expenses in the short term).
Return per Bottleneck Hour = Throughput per unit ÷ Bottleneck hours per unit.

TPAR = Return per Bottleneck Hour ÷ Cost per Bottleneck Hour (where Cost/hr = Total Factory Costs ÷ Total Bottleneck Hours).
TPAR > 1 means product generates throughput faster than factory costs are incurred; TPAR < 1 loses money unless improved.

front: Hansen & Mendoza Environmental Cost Categories (4 Types)
back:
1. Prevention costs (designing clean processes)
2. Appraisal/Detection costs (testing, environmental audits)
3. Internal failure costs (scrap, toxic waste treatment inside plant)
4. External failure costs (fines, remediation, reputational damage outside plant).

Input/Output Analysis: reconciles physical material purchased vs finished output + waste (mass balance).
Flow Cost Accounting: separates material, system, and delivery/disposal flows into positive products vs negative waste.

Must be Future, Incremental, and Cash flow.
Ignore: Sunk costs, committed costs, notional costs, absorbed fixed overheads, depreciation.

front: Relevant Cost of Existing Inventory Material
back:
1. If in regular use -> Current replacement cost.
2. If no other use -> Higher of net realisable value (scrap/resale) or opportunity cost of alternative use (or saved disposal cost if toxic).

Spare capacity (paid anyway) -> $0.
Full capacity (hire new/overtime) -> Incremental hourly/overtime cost.
Diverted from other work -> Direct labour cost + Lost contribution per hour of diverted product.

front: Multi-Product Breakeven & Weighted Average C/S Ratio
back:
Weighted Avg C/S Ratio = Total Budgeted Contribution ÷ Total Budgeted Sales Revenue.
Breakeven Revenue = Total Fixed Costs ÷ Weighted Avg C/S Ratio.
Margin of Safety (%) = (Budgeted Sales − Breakeven Sales) ÷ Budgeted Sales × 100%.

Rank products by Contribution per unit of Limiting Factor (or Throughput per Bottleneck Hour in Throughput Accounting).
Make-or-Buy with limiting factor: rank by Cost Saved per unit of scarce resource when making in-house vs buying.

front: Linear Programming: Slack vs Shadow Price
back:
Slack: unused amount of a non-binding constraint at the optimal vertex (Shadow price = $0).
Shadow Price: maximum extra contribution earned per 1 additional unit of a binding scarce resource (above its normal purchase cost).

P = a − bQ where b = ΔPrice ÷ ΔQuantity.
MR = a − 2bQ.
Profit is maximised where Marginal Cost (MC) = Marginal Revenue (MR). Solve for Q, then substitute into P = a − bQ.

front: Market Skimming vs Market Penetration Pricing
back:
Skimming: high initial price for innovative/inelastic early adopters, lowered later.
Penetration: low initial price to gain rapid market share and economies of scale when demand is elastic.

front: Decision Criteria under Uncertainty (Maximax, Maximin, Minimax Regret)
back:
Maximax (Optimist): choose highest of the best payoffs.
Maximin (Pessimist): choose highest of the worst payoffs.
Minimax Regret (Sore loser): build regret table (best in state − outcome), choose smallest maximum regret.
VOPI = Expected Value WITH Perfect Information − Expected Value WITHOUT Perfect Information (max EV).

Incremental: prior year budget + % adjustment (quick, breeds slack).
ZBB: start from zero, build Decision Packages ranked by cost/benefit (eliminates slack, time-consuming).

Rolling: continuously updated by adding a new quarter/month as the current one expires (ideal in uncertain environments).
ABB: works backwards from budgeted sales/production to activity drivers and cost pools.

Y = cumulative average time per unit for x units; a = time for 1st unit; b = log(learning rate) / log(2).
Total time for x units = x · Y.
Time for nth unit = Total time(n) − Total time(n−1). Learning stops at steady state!

front: Time Series: Trend, Seasonal Variation & Cyclical
back:
Additive: Y = T + S.
Multiplicative: Y = T × S (seasonal indices average to 1.0 or 100%).
Coefficient of Determination (r²): proportion of variation in y explained by x.

front: Materials Mix Variance vs Materials Yield Variance
back:
Mix Variance = (Actual Qty in Std Mix − Actual Qty in Actual Mix) × Std Price per kg.
Yield Variance = (Std Qty for Actual Output − Actual Total Qty at Std Mix) × Std Weighted Avg Price (or Std Cost per output unit).

front: Sales Mix Variance vs Sales Quantity Variance
back:
Use Standard Margin (under absorption) or Standard Contribution (under marginal).
Mix = (Actual Sales at Actual Mix − Actual Sales at Std Mix) × Std Margin.
Quantity = (Actual Sales at Std Mix − Budgeted Sales) × Std Margin.

Planning variance = (Original Std − Revised Std) × Revised/Actual volume (uncontrollable environmental shift).
Operational variance = (Revised Std − Actual) × Actual volume (controllable by operational manager).

front: Return on Investment (ROI) vs Residual Income (RI)
back:
ROI = Controllable Profit ÷ Capital Employed × 100%. Risk: dysfunctional rejection of projects above cost of capital but below current division ROI.
RI = Controllable Profit − (Capital Employed × Cost of Capital %). Avoids dysfunctional behaviour; harder to compare divisions of different sizes.

Minimum TP (Selling Division) = Marginal Cost + Lost Contribution per unit from external sales displaced.
Maximum TP (Buying Division) = External Market Price (or Net Marginal Revenue).
When spare capacity exists: Min TP = Marginal Cost.

front: Fitzgerald & Moon Building Block Model (Service Businesses)
back:
Dimensions: Results (Financial, Competitiveness) & Determinants (Quality, Flexibility, Resource Utilisation, Innovation).
Standards: Ownership, Achievability, Equity.
Rewards: Clarity, Motivation, Controllability.

front: Value for Money (VFM) 3Es in Not-for-Profit / Public Sector
back:
Economy: acquiring inputs of required quality at lowest cost.
Efficiency: maximising output per unit of input.
Effectiveness: achieving overall strategic outputs and outcomes.

Simultaneity/Inseparability (produced & consumed together), Heterogeneity (variability in human delivery), Intangibility (cannot touch before purchase -> rely on physical cues), Perishability (cannot store unsold capacity like empty hotel rooms/clinic slots).
